snapshot.title: SSC Science: Chemistry — Acids, Bases & Salts
snapshot.exam_hook: ⚡ SSC Science Hook: Vinegar: Acetic. Ant: Formic. Baking: Bicarbonate. Washing: Carbonate. POP: Sulfate. pH < 7: Acid.

quick_notes.title: Acids
quick_notes.detail: Sour, turn Blue litmus RED. pH < 7. Release H+ ions. Strong : HCl, H2SO4 (King of Chemicals). Weak : Acetic acid.
quick_notes.explanation: Acids are chemical substances that taste sour and have a pH value lower than 7, where pH is a scale from 0 to 14 that measures how acidic or basic a substance is. When you dip blue litmus paper, which is a special paper used to test acidity, into an acid, the paper turns red. Acids release hydrogen ions, written as H+, when dissolved in water, and these ions are what give acids their properties. Strong acids, like hydrochloric acid (HCl) and sulfuric acid (H2SO4, often called the King of Chemicals because it is used in many industrial processes), completely break apart in water to release many H+ ions. Weak acids, like acetic acid found in vinegar, only partially release H+ ions, making them less harsh.

quick_notes.title: Bases
quick_notes.detail: Bitter, soapy, turn Red litmus BLUE. pH > 7. Release OH- ions. Examples : NaOH (Caustic Soda), Mg(OH)2 (Milk of Magnesia - Antacid).
quick_notes.explanation: Bases are a group of chemical substances that have a bitter taste and feel slippery or soapy to the touch. When you dip red litmus paper, which is a special paper used to test chemicals, into a base, the paper turns blue. Bases have a pH value greater than 7, where pH is a scale from 0 to 14 that measures how acidic or basic a substance is. In water, bases release hydroxide ions (OH-), which are negatively charged particles that make the solution basic. Common examples include sodium hydroxide (NaOH), also called caustic soda and used in drain cleaners, and magnesium hydroxide (Mg(OH)2), known as milk of magnesia, which is used as an antacid to neutralize stomach acid.

quick_notes.title: Natural Acids (Memorize!)
quick_notes.detail: Vinegar (Acetic), Lemon (Citric), Tomato (Oxalic), Tamarind (Tartaric), Curd (Lactic), Ants (Formic/Methanoic).
quick_notes.explanation: Natural acids are sour-tasting substances found in plants, animals, and insects. For example, vinegar contains acetic acid, which gives it a sharp taste. Lemon juice has citric acid, making it sour. Tomatoes contain oxalic acid, while tamarind has tartaric acid, which gives it a tangy flavor. Curd, or yogurt, contains lactic acid, which makes it slightly sour. Ants produce formic acid, also called methanoic acid, which causes the sting or irritation when they bite.

quick_notes.title: Indicators
quick_notes.detail: Litmus (Lichen), Turmeric, Phenolphthalein (Pink in Base, colorless in Acid), Methyl Orange.
quick_notes.explanation: Indicators are substances that change color to show whether a solution is acidic or basic. Litmus, made from a living organism called lichen, turns red in an acid and blue in a base. Turmeric, a yellow spice, turns reddish-brown in a base and remains yellow in an acid. Phenolphthalein is a chemical indicator that becomes pink in a base and has no color in an acid. Methyl orange is another chemical indicator that turns red in an acid and yellow in a base.

quick_notes.title: Important Salts
quick_notes.detail: Washing Soda (Na2CO3.10H2O), Baking Soda (NaHCO3), Bleaching Powder (CaOCl2), Plaster of Paris (CaSO4.1/2H2O).
quick_notes.explanation: Washing soda, whose chemical formula is Na2CO3.10H2O, is a white crystalline solid used for cleaning clothes and softening hard water because it removes calcium and magnesium ions. Baking soda, or NaHCO3, is a white powder that releases carbon dioxide gas when heated, which is why it is used in baking to make cakes rise and also in antacids to neutralize stomach acid. Bleaching powder, with the formula CaOCl2, is a yellowish-white powder used to bleach cotton and linen in textile mills and to disinfect drinking water in water treatment plants. Plaster of Paris, written as CaSO4.1/2H2O, is a white powder that, when mixed with water, forms a hard solid; it is used by doctors to make casts for broken bones and by artists to make sculptures.

topic_title: SSC Science: Chemistry — Acids, Bases & Salts
lesson_intro: Today we study the 'Chemistry of Reactions'. Acids and Bases are part of our daily life—from the lemon in your tea to the soap you use. In SSC, 'Natural Sources' (e.g., Formic acid in Ants) and 'Common Names' (e.g., Washing Soda) are high-yield. Do you know the pH of milk? Or why antacids are used for acidity? Let's master the reactive world today.
